 Timeline: Strong cold front hits Houston Sunday
 When the heaviest rain arrives and the severe weather threat you need to know about
 Anthony Yanez , Chief Meteorologist
 Daji Aswad , Meteorologist / Reporter
 Published:  November 13, 2026 at 7:18 PM Updated:  November 14, 2026 at 10:25 PM Tags:  Forecast , Cold front , Houston weather , Flood threat , Severe weather Houston watch for street ponding and flooding We have an important weekend forecast, and I want to walk you through what we’re going to see. Let’s start with the timing for Saturday. I think most of the day looks pretty good. 
 Saturday’s timing: 
 Saturday afternoon clouds begin to increase across southeast Texas. By 6pm watch for isolated showers and by 8 pm rain chances turn spotty to scattered. The better chance for showers start after sunset. 
 Showers move into southeast Texas Sunday’s timing 6:00 AM: 
 As people are starting their Sunday, expect to see scattered rain in the Houston area. The strongest thunderstorms are north of southeast Texas. 
 Scattered rain across southeast Texas ahead of cold front Sunday afternoon 12:00 PM: 
 Widespread heavy rain moves into Houston Sunday afternoon. There are some severe weather parameters that are coming together, and if they can line up, we could get severe weather at this time. Make sure you have a back up plan Sunday afternoon and evening. 
 Widespread rain and embedded storms as fronts moves through southeast Texas Severe weather threat: 
 While the threat is low, hail, damaging winds and a tornado are possible. Our far northern and northeastern cities do not have as much energy in the atmosphere for strong storms. The rest of us in green are under a low threat. 
 Hail, damaging winds and a tornado is possible (Copyright 2026 by KPRC Click2Houston - All rights reserved.) There is also a Wind Advisory for southern counties from 9 AM to 3 PM Sunday. Gust could blow over 30 mph.
 Jackson, Matagorda, Brazoria, Galveston, Chambers counties could have winds up to 35 mph Street flooding possible: 
 From The Woodlands south, flooding for low-lying areas and areas with poor drainage, as well as minor street flooding is possible. 
 2/4 across Harris county Rain totals: 
 The graphic does a good job of showing the range in rain totals through Sunday. If too much rain falls in a short amount of time, we’ll get flooding. 
 1" to 4" is the general range (Copyright 2026 by KPRC Click2Houston - All rights reserved.) Sunday night 6:00 PM: 
 By the time we get to 6:00, the storms are off the coast with lingering showers left in southeast Texas through Monday. A colder and windy day arrives Monday. Be safe and if you get any good pictures of the storms please send them to www.click2pins.com .
